💡 Key Takeaways
  • When comparing free weights and gym machines, I am firmly on the side of free weights.
  • There are other benefits, too, like building stability, coordination, balance and range of motion, but I use certain gym machines like cables or leg presses, and I may start a beginner on certain machines until they feel more confident with the movements.
  • All of this is to say, there's one piece of equipment I avoid for core exercises, particularly sit-ups, because more often than not, I see people in the gym getting injured.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When comparing free weights and gym machines, I am firmly on the side of free weights. Equipment like dumbbells and kettlebells allows you to work both sides of your body independently, while using barbells means you can load heavy, working your core muscles harder to stabilize you without the help and support of a machine.

There are other benefits, too, like building stability, coordination, balance and range of motion, but I use certain gym machines like cables or leg presses, and I may start a beginner on certain machines until they feel more confident with the movements.

All of this is to say, there's one piece of equipment I avoid for core exercises, particularly sit-ups, because more often than not, I see people in the gym getting injured.

Read on for the full lowdown, and what to do instead.

It has been revealed that the GHD machine, or Glute Ham Developer as it was originally designed, can be used (and is commonly used) for sit-ups. The GHD sit-up is an intense sit-up variation used to improve core strength, stability and hip mobility, as it requires excessive and full range of motion as you lean back.

Industry observers note that although your hip flexors help power the torso upward, they shouldn't take over the exercise, which targets the abs running along the front of your stomach. The problem is, the excessive range of motion can load the lower back, and if you don't perform the exercise properly, with enough core engagement, or if you right now have a health condition (like high or low blood pressure), are pre- or post-natal, or have an injury, this exercise quickly becomes contraindicated.

For this reason, I skip the GHD machine for core exercises, especially for beginners, as repeated lumbar flexion and extension of the spine in an unsupported position offers more problems, in my opinion, than benefits.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Here's what I recommend instead.

According to recent reports, you need a lot of power to drive your body to a sitting position, so the first thing I'll do is get someone on a pull-up bar for hanging leg raises or knee tucks. L-sits are also a great option for developing deep core strength while also targeting the hip flexors and grip strength.

Although your back is still unsupported, you're putting a lot less strain on your spine while still building strength in your upper body.

If you're determined to use a GHD machine, I recommend relearning to brace your core using my five-minute bracing routine. Core engagement isn't just about squeezing your stomach hard or sucking your belly in; it's about gently bracing the abdomen and bearing down, as if someone is about to punch you in the gut. You'll also need to exhale as your body meets the most resistance, which means as you sit up in this case.

Recent findings suggest that finally, did you know your diaphragm is a core muscle? Breathing properly requires diaphragmatic breathing, which means directing your breath downward rather than out through your chest.

I strongly recommend spending some time activating your core and diaphragm first, and trying some pelvic tilts to get everything fired up beforehand while supporting your spine.

If possible, I would use dumbbells, Bosu trainers, resistance bands, kettlebells, or Swiss balls over going anywhere near the GHD machine.

You can slowly overload the body as you get stronger, adding weight or volume as you develop core strength and stability. Bosu trainers test balance and stability, and kettlebells increase range of motion as you can move them more freely.

Free weights are also far more functional than many gym machines, as you teach your muscles to support you rather than relying on a piece of kit. This is extremely beneficial for your core, which in turn is better for your back health.

Industry observers note that movements that are functional should also feel natural, aiding everyday activities. Plus, you should feel like you have far more control.

It has been revealed that you put a lot of trust into the GHD when doing one of these sit-ups. Your entire body is held by the two rollers that clamp around your feet. It's not for everyone.

There's an extensive library of exercises that benefit your body more, and it's a great opportunity to experiment with what does and doesn't work for your body.

I would start with these 5 Pilates exercises and some lower abs workouts.

I also really rate endurance-focused core exercises that use isometric contraction, which means you hold tension in the working muscles without them lengthening or shortening. Examples include the hollow hold (pictured above) and plank variations.

It has been revealed that I don't know many people who get away with zero pain using the GHD machine, and it might be a lack of core engagement, weakness in the stabilizing muscles, existing back pain, poor technique, or something as simple as body mechanics. For me, I just don't think it's worth the risk.

Breaking: Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as 'biggest breakthrough in decades'

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing.
  • A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades.
  • Sources indicate that in one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib, during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing.

A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades.

Sources indicate that in one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib, during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. The trial participants had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body.

Though doctors have mentioned the pill cannot yet be considered a cure, and they do not know how long it can keep the disease at bay, they have said it is encouraging news because it appears it will offer patients more time, even if it does not cause full remission.

Industry observers note that half of all people diagnosed with pancreatic cancer die within three months, and only about 3% of patients survive for five years when the disease spreads to other organs. It has the lowest survival rate of all common cancers in the UK and has a similarly poor prognosis globally.

Patients were followed for a year and a half during the trial on average and some did not see the cancer return during this period. Longer studies will be conducted to see if any of the cancers can be put into remission. During the trial, tumours stopped growing in 90% of patients, just over 60% of patients had their tumours shrink or disappear, and for about 8% of patients tumours became undetectable on CT scans.

A year after starting treatment, 76.6% of patients were alive; usually 40-45% of patients given chemotherapy alone survive a year.

Dr Wungki Park, a gastrointestinal medical oncologist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York, who presented the findings, said “this is the closest to cure”, adding that he had never seen so many tumours disappear in patients whose cancer had spread.

He presented the findings at the EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics in Barcelona. “We are beginning to see not only a higher percentage of tumour response rates, but also deeper responses and a near doubling in the duration of disease control, which may eventually translate into longer survival,” he noted.

Recent findings suggest that “The median follow-up is 18 months. Just imagine, in an average of 18 months your disease just disappears on the CT scan … that’s closest to complete remission … it’s incredible.”.

In a recent development, daraxonrasib is a KRAS inhibitor treatment, which works by locking on to and shutting off certain mutations found in most pancreatic cancers. These mutations drive tumour growth.

There are hopes the treatment could work for dozens of other cancers because they can have similar mutations.

Michelle Mitchell, Cancer Research UK’s chief executive, said more research was needed, but added: “This is the biggest leap forward we’ve seen in decades for pancreatic cancer patients and could offer real hope to people facing one of the deadliest and most difficult-to-treat cancers.

“These results raise the exciting possibility that this breakthrough could eventually pave the way for treating other cancers that carry Kras gene mutations. More trials are now needed before this treatment can be assessed for use on the NHS and despite this advance, pancreatic cancer survival is still very low.”.

5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1173 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, at the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities.
  • Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?
  • Industry observers note that the capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, at the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities. According to Google, this is now happening at scale.

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

Industry observers note that the capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate. Like it or not, AI has an integral role in the new reality — for the defenders and threat actors.

Speed and scale are the main reasons enterprises consider adopting AI in SOCs and for security more broadly, and these factors underpin Google’s latest security forecast for 2027 — Cloud CISO Perspectives. However, without the right precautions, AI security adopters could inadvertently increase their attack surface rather than shrink it.

With this in mind, these are five ways AI will change the security industry over the next year and what CISOs need to consider going into 2027.

Recent findings suggest that alert fatigue is well-known across SOC teams. Alert after alert needs to be trawled through; many are irrelevant or false positives, tying up skilled staff with the mundane, tedious, time-consuming task of triaging them.

Now that autonomous, AI-driven threats can probe a network, gain entry, and move laterally across it in minutes, chasing threat data and security alerts from multiple systems logged days or weeks ago can’t help a business mitigate them — and certainly not at the speed of the threat.

According to Google’s forecast, AI will mean the alert queue quietly disappears. Ramya Chitrakar, VP of engineering at Google Cloud Security, believes that “2027 is the year analysts stop chasing alerts and start shaping outcomes.”.

Also: AI is both a cyber weapon and a massive target.

How? CISOs must change the alert model itself. Instead of human defenders triaging alerts at the start of a cybersecurity incident, the alert becomes final output, with autonomous agents handling “data enrichment, correlation, and triage automatically, surfacing a verified conclusion rather than a raw ticket,” according to Google.

This means cybersecurity experts can oversee alert handling and verify automated actions, potentially freeing them to focus on other tasks.

According to recent reports, custom agentic AI is often designed — or at least intended — to work autonomously, with human oversight. However, having thousands of individual agents working across multiple environments can create high-value entry points into corporate networks that cyberattackers target.

We need to think of agentic AI as more than a tool: each one needs its own identity, like a human employee, to operate within a zero-trust architecture, retain control, and reduce the risk of compromise.

Also: Your enterprise AI access can be sold for pennies – beware ‘LLM Mixers’.

However, Heather Adkins, VP of security engineering at Google, thinks this needs to go further and suggests the zero-trust concept shouldn’t stop at the network layer. Instead, Adkins believes it needs to reach the transaction layer.

In a recent development, A paper trail for each agent needs to be established, which is impossible to handle manually, and even within a zero-trust framework, AI agents could be given too much scope. Instead, implement verification for each transaction and for every authorization, and assign each AI agent its own least-privilege set of credentials that can be revoked if there is a security incident or the agent is no longer required.

“When backed by real-time autonomous reasoning, we can dynamically allow a transaction on Tuesday and block the exact same request on Wednesday if conditions look anomalous,” the report notes.

AI is being used to speed up the development and deployment of fresh software, and in 2027, security will have to become a continuous system embedded in the software delivery pipeline, according to Google.

It has been revealed that threat actors have carried out software supply chain attacks over the years, one of the most notable being the SolarWinds incident of 2020. Sandra Joyce, VP of Google Threat Intelligence, notes cybercriminals are now poisoning everything from open-source code to software libraries, which AI coding assistants often pull automatically into codebases.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain.

Industry observers note that bug-fix tickets that take days to respond to and security appearing at the end of a software development cycle no longer work. Instead, writing and securing code must happen simultaneously, with the help of agentic AI, so speed doesn’t compromise security.

“It’s also crucial that we link live production environments directly back to source code so that defenders can trace a real-world exposure to the exact line of code, validate whether it is genuinely exploitable, and deliver a pre-tested fix at machine speed without breaking production,” Google added.

As organizations rush to implement AI into their applications and services to appear “AI-first,” innovative, and modern, security may be ignored or treated as an afterthought.

Recent findings suggest that as a result, we may face a fresh, broader attack surface than we realize, as AI introduces new security challenges, including software vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, bypasses, and indirect prompt injection attacks. Now that AI is also in the hands of all cyberattackers — from script kiddies to state-sponsored groups — auditing corporate networks and infrastructure is crucial.

Industry observers note that also: Who’s responsible for catching rogue AI agents? You are.

Penetration testing and red team exercises now need to cover agentic AI. This wasn’t in scope for many red teams only a few years ago, but now that businesses have run with the idea of implementing AI in their workflows, processes, and products, organizations need to identify and fix security challenges introduced by AI before threat actors take advantage of them.

CISOs should task pen testers with auditing before an autonomous workflow hits production, then combine the results with threat intelligence to ensure defenders have the information they need to bolster network defenses and harden classifiers against new and novel attacks.

The final significant trend we are likely to see in 2027 is tackling agent sprawl to create coordinated teams of AI agents that can rapidly handle security tasks at scale.

Single AI agents given general instructions won’t cut it when AI-assisted attackers can compromise endpoint devices, enter networks, move laterally, or start stealing data in a far shorter timeframe than before. Instead, CISOs should replace these “generalist” AI agents with specialized, orchestrated teams of AI agents that can meet the demands of defending against AI-driven attacks by employing specialist tooling and skill sets.

Also: AI agent kill switch urged by Okta-led alliance.

CISOs also need to ensure that each agent has its own domain training and understanding, memory, and dedicated tools, and can act on its own within set limits, with a central coordinator that knows when to hand a decision to a human. This requires oversight, but in return, organizations will avoid agent sprawl, which the tech giant believes is the next iteration of shadow IT and its associated threats.

Industry observers note that I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. In a recent development, if you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

Japan’s three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according to Automotive News. The outlet reports that Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Koji Sato, who is also the vice chairman of Toyota, confirmed the decision at a news conference in Tokyo this week.

In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has looks to move to more components that cover the entire car. The three areas were chosen as the first to be standardized because they are parts that are generally not noticed by consumers, and they shouldn’t have an impact on any brand’s individual identity. All three are also areas that account for significant production costs for the automakers, meaning they can have an immediate impact.

The push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan’s seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. The automakers are mentioned to hope that they can channel the money saved by homogenizing into fresh innovations.

According to recent reports, “We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change,” Sato said. “Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in the press release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is exploring how people use AI for their health, presumably to build its own AI health coach. On Sunday, it launched the Apple Health AI Usage Study, which could contribute to the next AI health experience Apple builds by measuring the quality of AI health responses, comprehension, and everyday health behaviors, according to a press release.

Sources indicate that apple is conducting the study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals. The study examines the relationship between conversational AI tools, like chatbots, and the people who use them.

“Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in the press release.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

Recent findings suggest that participants are encouraged to share their HealthKit data and query the health app with questions. The study will also explore how AI tools can best prepare patients ahead of clinical visits. Apple will monitor the AI’s clarity and approachability when providing medical information, and each response or recommendation will be linked to peer-reviewed clinical citations. Responses could be unclear or incomplete, which is why Apple is rolling this out as a study to explore a responsibly designed AI health assistant.

Industry observers note that apple often rolls out studies for features it would like to develop in the future. For example, many of the hearing health features rolled out on the AirPods were a direct result of the findings from Apple’s Hearing Study.

Also: Athenahealth patients can ask Claude about their medical records now.

Recent findings suggest that the AI usage study comes on the heels of the revamped Health app’s debut, which launches officially next month. It also arrives amid a bevy of AI health coaches, popping up alongside companion health devices. Google debuted its AI Health Coach in Google Health Premium last year, and Oura launched a proprietary AI model for women trained on medical standards and research from Oura’s in-house team of board-certified clinicians.

A growing number of Americans are relying on AI for medical advice. A recent survey from Pew Research Center found that 34% of US adults have talked with a chatbot for medical advice. As AI proliferates, that percentage will only increase.

“Patients and clinicians are both turning to AI, but the tools they use are being built and tested in separate worlds,” mentioned Robert M. Wachter, M.D., UCSF’s professor and chair of the Department of Medicine, in the press release.

Apple and other tech companies are building for this fresh health normal, and the AI usage study indicates that Apple isn’t taking the responsibility lightly.

Industry observers note that if you’re interested in participating in Apple’s study, it’s open to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older in the US. You’ll need a phone with Apple Intelligence enabled (the iPhone 15 Pro or later), running iOS 26 or later. You can download the study app to learn more and enroll.

Sources indicate that hey Siri, what’s the name of this blue plant on my screen? You couldn’t ask your iPad that question before, but you’ll be able to soon.

In its newly introduced iPadOS 27.3 release, Apple is adding several new features for iPads — Siri mode in the camera app, window resizing by tapping and more tools in the Freeform whiteboard app. The features are being tested in beta and will be released to the general public sometime in December. The new OS will be available on all iPads that support iPadOS 27.

The release notes for iPadOS 27.3 are listed here.

In a recent development, on an iPhone, you can ask Siri about what’s in your camera frame. Siri can identify the object and perform a web search on it. You can also take action items, such as pointing the camera at a restaurant bill and asking Siri to split it if you want to split it with people you’re with.

In a recent development, that same functionality will soon be available on iPads, with the iPadOS 27.3 release. Maybe you want to identify a plant out in nature, or an historic building during a walking tour, or figure out how to replicate a tasty dish you just ordered at a restaurant.

Another new feature in iPadOS 27.3 will make it easier to make windows bigger. Let’s say you’ve got a few windows open on your iPad, but there’s one you want to enlarge. You’ll be able to double-tap the top of the window to enlarge it, then double-tap again to revert it to its original size.

Prior to the iPadOS 27.3 release, you had to drag a corner of the window to make it bigger or smaller.

It has been revealed that freeform is an iPad app that serves as a digital whiteboard for sketching and writing out ideas and collaborating. You can add photos, videos, text, PDFs and other items to the whiteboard — using your mouse, finger or Apple Pencil — and sync it across other Apple devices such as iPhones and Macs.

I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip enhancement, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the new S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Sources indicate that everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

In a recent development, the new Health Sensing System makes Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.

Because of the new health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:.

The complications let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face. These are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.

I’ve been using the watchOS 27.3 beta, which adds a new Siri Recap feature for Series 12 models that I really love.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.

Most of what Siri documents, I’ll never need to reference and it gets deleted automatically. But for those times I have trouble remembering a key piece of information, I’ve found Siri Recap a very convenient addition.

Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.

Recent findings suggest that more battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:.

In a recent development, I wear my Apple Watch to bed and generally try to top it off swiftly in the evening, but I’m not always great at giving it much time on the charger. With faster charging support on Series 12, my poor planning isn’t a problem.

Apple Watch Series 12 is now only $329 on Amazon, down from $399.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Oura developed a tool for its frequent-flying members that could help them stave off the worst of jet lag.
  • Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, on Tuesday, Oura declared Jet Lag Plan, a upcoming feature designed to help travelers feel alert and energized after crossing several time zones.
  • Also: Oura Ring consumers may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oura developed a tool for its frequent-flying members that could help them stave off the worst of jet lag.

Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, on Tuesday, Oura declared Jet Lag Plan, a upcoming feature designed to help travelers feel alert and energized after crossing several time zones.

Also: Oura Ring consumers may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know.

Jet Lag Plan takes into account your travel itinerary, sleep patterns, and body responses to provide guidance for traveling members entering fresh time zones.

Jet lag happens when circadian rhythms are at odds with local time zones, but there are a few things people can do to adjust.

Oura factors in the direction of travel, how many time zones are crossed, individual light windows, and sleep timing.

Ring users will enter their flight details, including information like multi-stop trips, and also include the reason for the trip. Oura adjusts the Jet Lag Plan accordingly, and a business trip’s plan may differ in intensity from that of a vacation.

“Two people on the same flight can get different intends, because guidance reflects your itinerary, your typical sleep schedule, and your chronotype,” Oura writes in a blog post. The chronotype refers to Oura’s sleep chronotype, which categorizes users into six types (early morning, morning, early evening, and so on) based on their historical sleep activity.

Also: I wore the Oura Ring 5 for a month.

After adding these details, Oura provides each user with timely guidance throughout their trip. This guidance could include recommendations on when to begin or end caffeine consumption or light exposure, and when to start preparing for sleep. The plan is designed for those crossing three or more time zones. Members can follow along with these recommendations by checking them off as they complete each one. Owners can also talk to Oura’s Advisor in the event of flight or timing changes.

Jet Lag Plan is now available for Oura Members with Oura Ring Gen 3 or later.

Go to your home screen, tap the + and select Jet Lag Plan to get started. You can also tell Oura Advisor about a trip to initiate Jet Lag Plan. If the Oura app detects a time zone shift of 3 or more hours, Jet Lag Plan may appear as a push notification.

GTA 6 Launch Day Hits Different for Fired Rockstar Workers

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as people across the world sneak a day away from the office to play the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday, the Rockstar employees who made the game are hopefully enjoying a well-earned day off in celebration. But not everyone who worked on the cultural juggernaut is joining the victory lap.

For the 34 workers based in the UK and Canada who Rockstar dismissed in October 2025, GTA 6 launch day isn’t the day of celebration it should’ve been.

“I should be with my team, taking a photo at every poster I can see, and be happy about it,” says Branimira Yordanova, who worked for three years in the lighting department at Rockstar North in Edinburgh, Scotland. “But it’s impossible because of how much hurt the firing has caused everyone.”.

Rockstar fired the workers on the spot — something that’s only legal in the UK in cases of gross misconduct — alleging that they’d shared confidential manufacturer information on a Discord server.

It has been revealed that the workers tell a different story. They say the firm had long been aware of the Discord server, and only fired them when it started to look as though their efforts to unionize might succeed. They believe they were made an example of.

On the evening before the game’s launch, I spoke with Yordanova and her former colleague Dayne Oram, a senior production coordinator who had been at Rockstar for seven years and was also affected by the dismissals, about how they were feeling about launch day.

“One of our fellow colleagues said it the best,” claims Yordanova. “What we’ll feel tomorrow is mourning what could have been, whether we want to or not.”.

For all those who are mourning, others among the fired workers still hold a candle for GTA. Jacob Jones, who spent one year as a game tester before taking a role as a designer on the open world team for four years, was raring to play the game on launch day.

Jones graduated from being a childhood fan of the franchise – even counting the signatures of Rockstar co-founders Sam and Dan Hauser among his merch collection – to his dream job. He remains a GTA fan to this day, but describes feeling a sense of “poignance” and “bittersweetness” toward the launch.

For Oram, Yordanova and Jones, GTA 6 eve was already a heavy day, even aside from the launch fever.

They’re all part of a case brought by the Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain on behalf of 23 former Rockstar North employees, who say they were unfairly dismissed for union activity. Hours before Oram and Yordanova spoke with me, a Glasgow employment tribunal had heard Rockstar’s closing submissions, which now leaves the fired workers in limbo as they wait for a verdict.

According to recent reports, rockstar North maintains that it fired the employees for gross misconduct. The tech giant didn’t respond to a request for further comment.

Oram, Yordanova and Jones all speak highly of their former colleagues and teams, but Oram calls the sacking a “traumatic experience.” Only Yordanova managed to secure alternative employment in the past 13 months. Jones notes for now he’s focused on getting justice.

Meanwhile, reminders of their former employer have been everywhere as the studio geared up to release perhaps the most highly anticipated game of all time. Billboards, buses and online ads have been impossible to avoid, leaving Yordanova feeling “devastated.”.

“I’ve genuinely had to make sure to avoid looking at it,” she notes. “It’s such a cool game, and to know that you worked on it, you feel a sense of pride and joy to see it out. But it’s like that sense of joy has been taken away from us in such a ruthless manner.”.

In a recent development, oram acknowledges having “mixed feelings” about the launch. It’s been fantastic watching video footage of people playing and reviewing the game, they say. At the same time, they’ve found it difficult not being able to celebrate the moment with their former team.

It has been revealed that the workers fired from Rockstar North had varying ideas about whether they wanted to celebrate the launch, or avoid it entirely. Jones is one of those who started playing the game as soon as he got home from the tribunal at 1 a.m. By the time we spoke on Thursday, he’d played around six or seven hours.

“I personally think it’s a masterpiece,” he states. Even though he worked on the game, he’s discovering surprises everywhere. “I haven’t completed it yet, but I do think it is probably the greatest game ever made.”.

Oram says that they planned to stick with watching streams of the game on launch day. “I’m probably not going to play the game for a little while, but I am looking forward to at least watching some people,” they say. Oram worked across so many bits of the game that there’s plenty they’re excited to see people discover.

Yordanova says she’s firmly in the avoidance camp. “I was really excited about playing the game in its official form because obviously when you work on it, you get to play it,” she says. “Even while we were in the office, there were parts I was really excited about – but I don’t think I’ll be playing it for the foreseeable future.”.

In a recent development, she hopes that one day her feelings will change, she adds. “But right now, that’s just not possible in any way.”.

Sources indicate that instead, she’ll be spending the day with friends who supported her over the last year. She aims to “dive into another art form” by seeing the stop-motion animated film Wildwood at the cinema, which particularly appeals to her as a lighting artist.

Sources indicate that many people playing GTA 6 around the world won’t be aware of what happened to Oram, Yordanova, Jones and their colleagues during the game’s development, but the affected workers would like people to know. “I understand people just want to focus on the joy, but I don’t think you can separate the launch with what happened,” says Yordanova.

Industry observers note that reflecting on what happened, Jones claims it’s such a shame the way things went down. “It was my absolute passion,” he says. “I just wish that the circumstances were different, and I would have loved to have still been there working on games. I wish I got to the end.”.

I tested the Apollo Dash vs. the Segway E3 Go, and this is the scooter I’d pick for my commute

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1292 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that for a lot of commuters who want an electric scooter to get to and from work, you don’t need a tricked-out ride that costs over $1,000 and keeps up with the Porsches on the road.
  • I’ve recently been testing two scooters — the Apollo Dash and the Segway E3 Go — which are made for commuters, and can be purchased for less than $600.
  • The Apollo Dash has a top speed of 22 MPH, a max range of 25 miles, and has a 600W motor and 480Wh battery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for a lot of commuters who want an electric scooter to get to and from work, you don’t need a tricked-out ride that costs over $1,000 and keeps up with the Porsches on the road. Something much more modest — and affordable will do the trick.

I’ve recently been testing two scooters — the Apollo Dash and the Segway E3 Go — which are made for commuters, and can be purchased for less than $600. I’ve found them to be fairly evenly matched, so to help you decide which is best for your needs, I’ve broken things down into a round-by-round comparison.

The Apollo Dash has a top speed of 22 MPH, a max range of 25 miles, and has a 600W motor and 480Wh battery.

The Segway E3 Go has a top speed of 20 MPH, a max range of 25 miles, a 400W motor, and front suspension.

The Apollo Dash is regularly priced at $699, but as of this writing, is on sale for $529 at Apollo.com; the Segway E3 Go is regularly $649, but for Black Friday, I've seen it on sale for $449.

In a recent development, both of these scooters cut a pretty sleek profile. I personally like the cleaner lines of the Apollo as it transitions from the downtube to the deck; Segway’s folding mechanism, as well as its front suspension, makes things look a little busier.

However, from a comfort standpoint, I liked the raked handlebars of the Segway over the Apollo, and the fact that the turn signal switch is located by your left thumb. By comparison, the Dash requires you to use your right thumb to activate the right turn signal, which means you have to take your thumb off the throttle.

In a recent development, the display is one area where Segway and Apollo really differ; the E3 Go has a more traditional color LCD screen that demonstrates your speed and battery life. The Dash, on the other hand, uses a grid of white LEDs, which also shows your speed and battery life in a more basic way. However, The Apollo Dash also has a quad lock mount just below, so if you have a compatible phone case, you can use your phone as a digital dashboard.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

I like the folding mechanism on both scooters; you can collapse them in mere seconds, but I'm giving the advantage here to Segway. You can simply press on a flap with your foot, so you don't have to lean down.

Apollo’s scooter is slightly lighter than Segway’s — 43 pounds as opposed to 46.7 pounds. You’re going to get a workout either way.

In a recent development, one of my biggest concerns as a rider is being seen by other drivers. The Apollo’s large light bar, which extends the length of the downtube, makes you far more noticeable at night. In addition, you can adjust the angle of its headlight. By comparison, the Segway’s headlight is fixed, and it has no other lights in the front.

Both scooters have turn signals in the handlebars; however, only Apollo lets you adjust how long they remain on; from within the app, you can set a period from seven seconds or until you deactivate it.

I still wish both had turn signals in the rear of the scooter too, like the Segway Max G3 Plus or the Apollo City.

In a recent development, on my steep hill test (which has a max grade of 10%), the Segway slowed down to 4 MPH on the steepest section; I had to do a little wiggling of the handlebars to keep it balanced. By comparison, the Apollo managed to get up the same hill at 8 MPH — not exactly a speed record, but it was twice as fast as the Segway.

On a hill with a less steep grade of 5.7%, both scooters performed about the same, slowing to around 12 MPH.

According to recent reports, the raked handlebars, front suspension, and larger tires of the Segway E3 Go really made a difference, especially at speed. The scooter felt more stable when I was cruising at 20+ MPH, and was much less jarring than the suspension-less Apollo when I went over bumps and potholes.

Sources indicate that both the Apollo and Segway are rated for a max distance of 25 miles, but that’s assuming ideal conditions, and if you poke along at around 9 MPH on a flat road. With both scooters at full charge, Segway estimated that it had 11.2 miles of range, compared to 17 for the Apollo when both were set to their max performance levels. If you want to eke out a bit more range, both scooters offer regenerative braking.

I took them one at a time on an identical 5.5-mile loop around my town, going up and down the same hills. After a 5.5-mile ride, the Apollo had 55% battery left, while Segway’s had just 32%.

Now, range will vary greatly from one rider to another, but I suspect that the more powerful motor in the Apollo scooter enabled it to use power more efficiently during my test.

In a recent development, both Segway’s and Apollo’s apps let you customize how the scooter performs, to a certain extent. For example, with each, you can specify the max speed for each performance setting, so if you don’t want to zoom along at 20 MPH in Sport mode, you don’t have to.

It has been revealed that however, Apollo’s app offers a bit more customization. You can, for instance, set the amount of time that the turn signals remain on, and also fine-tune the throttle response, if you want to get off to a faster start.

According to recent reports, after testing both the Apollo Dash and the Segway E3 Go, neither really pulls away from the other to make this a decisive victory. Still, over these seven rounds, the Apollo Dash takes this matchup, winning four rounds to the Segway E3 Go’s three.

Industry observers note that I liked the design of the Segway’s handlebars and controls, and it felt more comfortable and stable while riding. And, at the time of this writing, it was $80 cheaper. However, the Apollo Dash proved more capable when scooting up hills, its lighting makes it far more visible, and it had a better range in my testing.

If you don't have hills to climb, then the Segway would be the better pick, but if you're facing some inclines, then I would lean towards the Apollo.

Recent findings suggest that in iOS 27, Apple revealed iPhone Handoff, a networking feature that allows consumers to switch cell service between two eSIM-enabled iPhones. Text strings in Google’s SIM Manager app suggest the company is preparing a similar feature for compatible Android phones, according to Android Authority.

Code strings include “Use a SIM on two phones,” and note that the feature will be called Fast Switch. Little information is currently available about the feature’s limitations, including which phones or mobile carriers may not be compatible.

Also: Why your USB-C cables look alike, but work differently – and how to tell them apart.

Sources indicate that on Apple’s side, any iPhone in the US running iOS 27 with a T-Mobile or Verizon-provided eSIM can use iPhone Handoff. AT&T does not right now support iPhone Handoff.

However, the code strings uncovered by Android Authority show that Android’s Fast Switch will work similarly to iPhone Handoff, in that users must be signed in to both devices under the same Google account for the feature to work.

Strings in Google’s SIM Manager app also point to no sharing between two customers, so this feature isn’t a way to circumvent carrier fees by adding service to someone else’s phone for the price of one.

Industry observers note that if Fast Switch works anything like iPhone Handoff, which it appears it will, one eSIM can be switched between two phones. So, calls, messages, location services, and other information synced to your Apple ID can remain consistent between two devices.

Also: 5 hidden iOS 27 features that make older iPhones better.

Some third-party apps, like banking, communications, or social media, may also remain consistent across the two phones, depending on the app’s syncing behavior.

Features like Apple’s iPhone Handoff and Google’s Fast Switch are ideal for people who regularly use two phones. Business owners and digital creators may want one phone strictly for business purposes and the other for personal use.

Also: Google Wallet turns your Android phone into a digital house key.

In that case, one person can keep up with two phones without paying for two phone service lines through their carrier. Still, users will incur a fee, as T-Mobile charges $5/month for iPhone Handoff, while Verizon charges $10/month.

Among iOS 27’s many new features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

With iOS 27, Apple introduces massive AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting fresh features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the update also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:.

Sources indicate that after iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

Recent findings suggest that to move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

According to recent reports, most users will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

I feel like I’m exactly who this feature was made for. After years of running dual SIM, I now have a personal line on my Duo and work line on an 18 Pro. Going out with friends, family, etc, I’d love to bring one phone again while bringing both numbers with me, but keeping work system access to a specific, separate device. Only current problem is waiting for Verizon to activate the feature and then see if it actually works well.

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums.
  • It has been revealed that we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics.
  • In a recent development, apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple people saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums. It’s also a good time to shop for a newly introduced laptop, but not every brand is worth your time and money.

It has been revealed that we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics. Our readers could choose from many popular laptop brands, but one was a clear favorite. It claimed eight awards, including the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Pick award. And it’s the one worth heavily considering if you plan to buy a latest laptop while there are holiday savings.

In a recent development, apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple people saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop. In comparison, 22.5% say they’re satisfied — bringing Apple to a near-perfect overall satisfaction score of 96.7%.

According to recent reports, apple’s overall impression also speaks to other awards it wins from CNET readers, including high ratings for its impressive battery life, display quality and high-quality build. All of those categories and more sum up Apple’s brand loyalty nod, with 68% of MacBook owners saying they would buy the same laptop and model from Apple again.

Recent findings suggest that how much are people paying for MacBooks? CNET found that 43.5% of Apple owners paid at least $1,500. Until earlier in 2026, the MacBook Air was Apple’s entry-level laptop, priced at least $1,299. The introduction of the budget-friendly MacBook Neo brought that down to a more reasonable $699. However, despite Apple’s laptops being more expensive than those from other brands, they still ranked high for their value proposition. Part of the reason for that is that MacBooks received high marks for hardware reliability. “Apple’s MacBooks might cost more than the average laptop, but their premium build quality means they’re built for the long haul,” said Matt Elliott, CNET’s laptop editor.

Recent findings suggest that if you plan to have your laptop for a while, you may be impressed by other features that make work easier and faster, like its M-series central processing unit for task management and AI capabilities, great battery life and a one-of-a-kind operating system — right now MacOS 27. All of the features and specifications bundled together make Apple’s perception as a high-end laptop worth the investment for long-term satisfaction.

Sources indicate that apple clinches a near-perfect score for its value perception. According to our survey results, 44% of Apple users said their MacBook has exceptional value. Others say their MacBook is worth what they paid for it (50.9%) — for a total positive score of 94.6%.

It has been revealed that digging deeper into Apple’s cost-to-value rating, 81.8% of Apple owners paid at least $1,000 for their laptops, which may seem costly, but Apple people seem OK with the price. That could be because, even though Apple has only three laptop models in a handful of sizes in its lineup, each one delivers solid performance and storage.

Recent findings suggest that take Apple’s proprietary processing chips, for example — each upgrade since the M1 release has improved the laptop’s speed, battery life and performance. Now the M6 can handle the MacBook’s AI capabilities, storage and high-resolution graphics. And for all of that power, most MacBooks are relatively thin and lightweight, making them easier for mobility — just a few of the reasons Apple users may be OK with paying more for what they’re getting.

It has been revealed that battery life is a major deal for many laptop buyers, and that’s another area where Apple delivers. Over a quarter of those surveyed (25.7%) said their MacBook’s battery life exceeds 10 hours — which is more than enough for a full day of work in most cases. And 18.7% say their MacBook’s battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours — totaling 44.4% of MacBook people saying their battery lasts 8 hours or more.

Comparatively, non-Apple laptop brands fall short in this category. Only 16.4% of Lenovo owners say their laptop’s battery lasts at least 8 hours, and even fewer for Dell (12.7%) and HP (11.8%). If you’re leaning toward a MacBook for its battery life, CNET’s lab test shows that the MacBook Neo lasts 13 hours and 26 minutes for online streaming, whereas the Apple MacBook Air 13-inch M5 (2026 model) lasts 17 hours and 2 minutes.

Apple sweeps the brightness, color accuracy and clarity category with 99.2% of its consumers either satisfied or extremely satisfied with their laptop’s screen performance. No Apple users reported dissatisfaction.

Industry observers note that “Apple has long been a favorite for creative professionals and content creators for good reason: Its MacBook displays are some of the best you’ll find on any laptop,” stated Josh Goldman, CNET’s managing editor for computers. “While Apple may use marketing names like Retina and Liquid Retina to describe display features, they do translate into sharp and clear text and images, with excellent brightness, contrast, color gamut coverage and color accuracy.”.

It has been revealed that the latest MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR even goes beyond what MacBook owners have come to expect. It’s Apple’s first OLED touchscreen laptop and features next-level brightness, color and contrast.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Also: 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers.
  • Apple hasn’t been shy about stating that the use of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for specific tasks would face daily access limits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, have you been using the fresh Siri AI? If so, how much? I’ve been turning to it a lot since the release of iOS 27. Well, how we use it — and how often — will soon depend on how much we pay for an iCloud+ strategy.

Also: 5 apps I need Siri AI to work with now that it’s open to third-party developers.

Apple hasn’t been shy about stating that the use of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence for specific tasks would face daily access limits. Increased limits would be granted based on your iCloud+ subscription. Now the company has revealed how much it will cost you and when the limits will begin.

“Starting with the 2027 software releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are available for free for customers with a supported device set to a supported language,” Apple said on a support page updated November 16. “Some features rely on powerful server models and have limits where increased access is available with eligible iCloud+ looks, starting with the 27.3 release.”.

iOS 27.3 is expected to launch in early December, so that’s when the daily usage limits will kick in.

At that point, people with no paid iCloud+ plan and even those with the $0.99-per-month 50 GB plan will be the most limited, with Apple saying only that they’ll face a “Standard Device Limit.”.

What is a standard limit? That depends not just on how many times you tap into Siri per day but on what tasks you assign it. Basic Siri commands, such as setting timers and alarms or sending standard text messages, will remain free and unlimited.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

Advanced Siri and Apple Intelligence tasks will bump into the usage limits. These include the following, according to Apple:.

It has been revealed that one positive here is that the limits are per device not per account. That means you can use Siri AI and Apple Intelligence with the same account across your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro without fear of chewing up too much of your quota.

This all sounds like a way for Apple to steer people to more expensive iCloud+ accounts. But the limits are in place for a key reason. Basic commands are processed on your device, so they don’t require the use of Apple servers. More advanced tasks are processed using server-side AI models, which can feel the strain if too many people access them all at once.

Also: What you’ll pay for AI agents will be wildly variable and unpredictable.

How will you know if you use up your daily allotment and what happens then? You’ll receive a notification if you hit your limit for a particular feature category. At that point, you can still give Siri basic tasks to perform. But advanced ones will be paused until your limit resets the next day. Otherwise, Apple is undoubtedly hoping that people who continually run into limits will upgrade to a pricier iCloud+ initiative.

Latest Update: Apple’s Support Community Shuts Down on Friday, Removing User Discussions

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (931 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations.
  • A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov.
  • In a recent development, apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations. For a few more hours, the website will remain read-only, but I’ve found the search function crashes intermittently, so even that ability isn’t very reliable.

A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov. 10, warning visitors that the site would shut down and be offline entirely on Friday. If you want to look up a specific Apple troubleshooting topic on iPhones or HomePods, you should do it this evening. Soon, the entire peer advice and support site, which has been operating for nearly three decades, will be gone.

In a recent development, apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998. For those of you who might remember, that’s the year Apple debuted its iMac G3, the desktop with a translucent blue teardrop-shaped case. The iMac G3 abandoned legacy ports and the floppy disc drive in favor of CD-ROM and USB.

It has been revealed that back then, the site was called Apple Tech Exchange, later renamed Apple Discussions until it eventually became the Apple Support Community in 2011. Many still turned to forums for DIY solutions, using it to get advice from other tinkerers interested in figuring out how to fix things on their own.

Recent findings suggest that an Apple spokesperson told CNET the decision was made “after careful evaluation of our strategy and our customers’ needs.” Apple’s site notification directs people to visit the official Apple Support site. You’ll also be able to use Apple’s online chat, support phone numbers and in-store support, the same way they worked in the past.

Apple is one of the first American tech companies to give up its community discussion site — Google still has Google Communities Help, and Amazon manages its own forum domain with discussions from both staff and consumers. But Apple’s sudden closure could indicate a major shift, with others eventually following suit. It has highlighted an ongoing discussion about the role of peer support in tech, how AI has changed our online conversations and more.

When news of the shutdown spread, Apple customers flocked to the internet to express everything from dismay to vindication.

Recent findings suggest that for many, the Apple Support Community forums were controversial, not least because it wasn’t always clear how they worked. The site contained “user-submitted content, comments and opinions” and was “for informational purposes only,” yet many would mistake it for official Apple Support from staff.

According to recent reports, in discussions on Reddit about the closure, many bemoaned the absence of real Apple employees from the site’s forums and found the advice from other Support Community users to often be frustrating and not worth the effort. On the unofficial Apple subreddit, many mourned the loss of community while also noting that answers on the forum were often much harder to come by. Others said the site grew less helpful over the years.

According to recent reports, CNET phone reviewer and senior editor Mike Sorrentino told me that the forum shutdown “will likely drive customers looking for help with basic questions to Apple’s official support articles rather than user-created threads.” But Sorrentino also acknowledged that the move reflects a general trend away from the site, with more people getting answers from sites like Reddit. “Apple’s always been massive on controlling what information is shown on its website, and in that view, moving away from user discussion makes sense,” he said.

It has been revealed that just this week, I used the Apple Support Community site when looking for an answer to a problem implementing Apple Intelligence on my home security cameras, which required jumping through multiple hoops. Perhaps tellingly, I ended up finding the correct answer on Reddit. But that could become harder to do in the near future.

Industry observers note that the shutdown of Apple’s peer support forums is definitely a sign of the times, especially as tech companies push users away from repairing their own devices and toward replacing them outright — or at least encourage device owners to pay for official support services. It’s also a sign of the growing role of artificial intelligence, which is capitalizing on user-created content to provide summaries, moving people away from organic discussion and exchange on sites like these.

Industry observers note that reddit has lucrative data-licensing contracts with Google and OpenAI, allowing the companies to train their AI models on Reddit’s massive archive of human discussions, as well as surface Reddit content in tools like Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT. Reddit is also moving to a login-only viewing mode, making it significantly harder for casual users to find answers unless they trust AI summaries.

Industry observers note that apple may be leery of keeping so much user knowledge online for AI models to scrape for their own answers. The firm may also want to prevent AI summaries from providing information from past forum users on how to jailbreak Apple devices or DIY fixes, even as the EU has mandated that Apple start building replaceable batteries by next year. And it wouldn’t be a good look if Siri AI started regurgitating incorrect or outdated info it had picked up from Apple’s own sites.

In a recent development, whatever the reason, the circle of Apple owners helping users has grown smaller, and that doesn’t bode well for support forums as a whole. It may be time to start archiving those years of data before other tech companies implement similar aims.

Should You Forget Nvidia and Buy These 2 AI Memory Stocks Instead?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (733 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia has grabbed all the headlines in recent weeks, mainly over what's going on with former CEO Jensen Huang.
  • One of the biggest investment opportunities in the market right now is in memory chip stocks, with Micron (MU -13.89%) and Sandisk (SNDK -16.05%) being the two best options.
  • There are many unknowns surrounding Nvidia right now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keithen Drury – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:03PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Micron Technology ›.

Nvidia has grabbed all the headlines in recent weeks, mainly over what's going on with former CEO Jensen Huang. This has pummeled the stock, but there are other stocks benefiting from the same tailwinds as Nvidia that don't have the same headline risk right now.

One of the biggest investment opportunities in the market right now is in memory chip stocks, with Micron (MU -13.89%) and Sandisk (SNDK -16.05%) being the two best options. But are they better than Nvidia? Let's take a look.

There are many unknowns surrounding Nvidia right now. Whether it's questions about how much of its chip sales may be going to China through third parties, or whether all of the demand was legitimate, nobody knows. However, one point that's not up for debate is that demand for AI computing is real, and it has stretched memory chip suppliers to their limits.

Sources indicate that both Micron and Sandisk have sold out of production capacity, and it could be that way for many years, despite both companies opening fresh facilities in the near future to raise capacity. Micron's management team told investors that it expects memory chip market conditions to be worse in 2027 and 2028 than in 2026, an incredible statement, given how bad things are right now. This will keep memory chip prices elevated for some time, which is fantastic news for investors.

In a recent development, both have a long history of being highly cyclical companies, with good times when demand is high and downturns when there is excess supply. Historically, these cycles don't last for much more than a year, and that's exactly what the market is expecting this time around.

However, with AI hyperscalers needing much more computing capacity, this build-out could last until 2030 or beyond.

That's a lot of time for both Sandisk and Micron to produce a ton of profits and reshape their futures, while also delivering huge investor returns on the way.

It has been revealed that they are doing this by reshaping their business models. Sandisk and Micron are starting to sign long-term agreements with their clients, which sets a floor and a ceiling on memory prices. While this cuts out some of the peaks, it prevents these two from going into deep downturns when demand isn't as high. That sets their businesses up for long-term success.

But can their returns trump Nvidia?

Because the market is expecting a cyclical downturn any day now, each of these stocks is valued at a dirt cheap level.

MU PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

With both stocks at about 4 times this year's projected earnings (both companies are already in fiscal year 2027), that's a huge discount to the broader market. Nvidia is also cheap at about 10 times next year's earnings, but that pales in comparison to these two.

This makes these two excellent options, but only if the market comes around to valuing them properly. If the market keeps these two at low valuations due to concerns about their cyclical nature, these stocks may be duds. However, I don't see that happening.

According to recent reports, both Sandisk and Micron have been repurchasing shares with their profits, which allows them to artificially boost earnings per share by decreasing the number of shares outstanding. This is nothing newly introduced and has been done successfully by many companies in the market.

Sources indicate that when I think about Adam Driver as an actor, two words come to mind: stoic and intense. I see a disciplined actor with no social media presence who lets his work speak for itself.

Part of that discipline comes from his military background, while the rest stems from his time at Juilliard. Driver would have loved to come up in the 1960s and 1970s, as he feels cut from the same cloth as Robert De Niro and Al Pacino.

Industry observers note that at the moment, Driver stars in “Paper Tiger,” James Gray’s Latest York City crime drama about two brothers whose business dealings become entangled with the Russian mob. Driver has received rave reviews for his performance, with some critics calling it the actor’s best work. In honor of “Paper Tiger,” here are Driver's five best movies.

Sources indicate that the irony of Driver’s career is that despite being known for his intensity, he’s extremely funny. Driver’s breakout role came as Adam Sackler in the HBO comedy “Girls.” Since this list concerns movies, I’ll select another project from that era: “What If,” or in some territories, “The F Word.” (“What If” is a better title, for what it’s worth.) One night, Wallace (Daniel Radcliffe) and Chantry (Zoe Kazan) meet and hit it off. Although Chantry has a boyfriend, Wallace elects to be her friend because he’s in love with her.

It has been revealed that wallace and Chantry seem perfect for each other, but bad timing and unfortunate circumstances keep them apart. Driver plays Allan, Wallace’s best friend. Allan is a boisterous friend who encourages Wallace to tell Chantry how he feels. “What If” is a charming rom-com with a hilarious performance from Driver, who deserves recognition for his line delivery in the “greatest moment of my life” speech.

Like many “Star Wars” fans, I have problems with the sequel trilogy. My biggest gripe is with “The Rise of Skywalker,” especially the entire Palpatine debacle. It’s difficult to tell the story of Driver’s career without a “Star Wars” movie, so I’ll go with “The Force Awakens,” the highly entertaining popcorn blockbuster that kicked off Lucasfilm’s Disney era. Thirty years after the events of “Return of the Jedi,” the galaxy faces a new Imperial threat: the First Order.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Industry observers note that the Resistance, led by General Leia Organa (Carrie Fisher), recruits a fresh set of rebels, including Poe Dameron (Oscar Isaac), Finn (John Boyega), and Rey (Daisy Ridley). Driver plays Kylo Ren, a ruthless warrior in the First Order out to find the location of Luke Skywalker. Driver’s intensity translates seamlessly to a villainous role. Kylo is Gen Z’s version of Darth Vader. Driver plays Ren as a brooding, sad boy with daddy challenges. It’s a subversion of masculinity and an interesting addition to the “Star Wars” lineup of iconic villains.

Industry observers note that spike Lee stated it best. While speaking with BBC Radio 1 for “BlacKkKlansman,” Lee described Driver as a “beast.” Lee went on to praise Driver’s range as an actor. No arguments here, Mr. Lee. In “BlacKkKlansman,” John David Washington stars as Ron Stallworth, the first Black detective in the Colorado Springs Police Department.

Looking to infiltrate the local Ku Klux Klan, Ron poses as a white supremacist over the phone. The Klan buys it and wants to meet Ron. Since he’s Black, Ron recruits his white Jewish co-worker, Flip Zimmerman (Driver), to pose as him. The ruse works, and the duo infiltrates the Ku Klux Klan to thwart its nefarious prepares. “BlacKkKlansman” is a witty and sharp critique of racism and extremist political movements.

It’s also a film that eerily resembles events from the current day, which is scary in itself. Driver’s grounded presence is the perfect counterbalance to Washington’s excessive charisma. Driver earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor, the first of his career.

It has been revealed that I enjoy Driver as a heel. He knows how to get under my skin as a villain. He did it in “Star Wars,” and he arguably did it better in “The Last Duel.” Ridley Scott’s period piece is based on the last trial by combat in medieval France. The movie is split into three parts, detailing the viewpoints of Jean de Carrouges (Matt Damon), Jacques le Gris (Driver), and Marguerite de Carrouges (Jodie Comer).

Marguerite accuses Jacques of rape while Jean is out of town. With no physical evidence, it becomes Marguerite’s word versus Jacques’s, with the latter vehemently denying the accusation. Believing he must defend his family's honor, Jean requests a duel to the death, which Jacques accepts.

Sources indicate that don’t let the box office failures turn you away from this excellent drama and Scott’s best movie this decade. It’s a shockingly violent movie, but also one that rewards patience. It’s not good vs. bad. Instead, it’s about morally complex characters, making for a far more interesting dilemma.

According to recent reports, if I were having trouble in a relationship, “Marriage Story” might be at the bottom of the pile of films to watch. Noah Baumbach’s drama about a couple going through a divorce features some of the meanest, rawest, and most emotional scenes I’ve ever seen. At times, it punches you in the heart and makes you question everything you knew about love. At the center of the movie are Charlie (Driver) and Nicole Barber (Scarlett Johansson), a married couple.

Charlie, a theater director, and Nicole, an actress, agree to a divorce. Charlie remains in Upcoming York, while Nicole heads to Los Angeles with their son, Henry (Azhy Robertson). The couple begins divorce proceedings cordially, but when lawyers get involved, it becomes cutthroat. Some of these scenes between Charlie and Nicole, especially the climactic argument, are like watching a car crash — you can’t look away. It’s an acting tour de force for Driver and Johansson, who earned their respective Oscar nominations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Gemini can now turn your notes and other sources in your Gemini Notebook (previously called NotebookLM) into interactive pages or sites to help you better process complicated information.

In a recent development, complete with flashcards, dashboards, and colorful panels, the sites make it easier to study and understand intricate concepts. I tested the feature, announced Tuesday, to see how efficient it is at creating a navigable site that is actually helpful and stays loyal to sources.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s upcoming Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector in my tests.

Because Notebooks are built with the sources you provide, like textbooks, files, or notes, the sites are created with the data that is in your Gemini Notebook. Notebook has three tabs: Sources, Chat, and Studio. The site option is in the Studio tab, listed under what you can create.

If you’re taking a college class, you could put all the information you need to prepare for a test and use the interactive site as a study guide that you can share with others.

To test this, I gave Notebook the following prompt:.

“Make me a site that visually explains how cellular respiration works, breaking down each stage with interactive diagrams and self-check flashcards.”.

Industry observers note that since I’m not in a class that would give me those study materials, I gave Gemini online sources to use for this. Gemini cited the sources in my notebook, then spent a few minutes creating the interactive site. Gemini will give you a quick revision when it’s done, including a summary of the source information as it pertains to your request and instructions on where to find the site.

Also: I checked Gemini’s upcoming Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

According to recent reports, as promised, my cellular respiration notes were complete and organized on an interactive, visually appealing site that was easy to navigate. The coolest feature on the site was the flashcards, which you can hover over to see which ones you’ve studied.

The interactive site feature is now available to Gemini Notebook users and will soon come to the mobile app. As someone who knows very little about coding, I was pretty satisfied to see the information Gemini put together presented in explorable, easy-to-understand tabs on a site.
