📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you picked up a new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo this fall, or you’re shopping for someone with an iPad, AirPods, or Apple Watch, there’s a good chance you’ve been holding out on purchasing accessories until all of the Black Friday deals started. We’ve got you covered with some great deals on premium accessories for nearly every Apple device on your list.

ESR has been making Apple accessories since 2009, and that track record has made it a trustworthy name for the more than 123 million people who use its products to protect their Apple devices and make them more versatile. Here’s a look at what’s included in ESR’s Black Friday lineup and who each one is for.

If someone on your shopping list picked up an iPhone Duo, a case is the first thing they need, and it’s also the hardest one to get right. As we’ve seen with Android foldables, you’re protecting two halves, a hinge, and a phone that changes shape throughout the day as you use it, all without adding bulk to a device people bought because it folds thin. ESR has two options for iPhone Duo owners, and the choice mostly comes down to the look you want to achieve.

The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand is your choice if you want to show off your iPhone Duo’s colors. It combines a rigid polycarbonate and acrylic back with a softer TPU frame. The rigid back keeps the case from flexing and lets the iPhone Duo’s design show through, while the flexible frame absorbs the shock if you drop it (please don’t).

The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand is perfect for those who want a more premium look for their iPhone Duo. It’s made from organic silicone leather with a soft, skin-friendly feel and a stain-resistant finish. If you’ve ever used a light-colored leather case before, you know it usually shows every stain and smudge it comes across, but ESR built the Atelier to resist daily wear and wipe clean.

According to recent reports, both cases share ESR’s Flex Stand, and it’s one of the most innovative and versatile parts of the lineup. It’s a 180-degree rotating stand made from zinc alloy, so it holds its shape even after months of propping up your iPhone. A precision hinge with damping control lets it open smoothly and lock at the angle you choose, whether the iPhone Duo is folded or unfolded, and ESR indicates it has passed 3,000 open-and-close tests. In real life, that means propping the iPhone Duo open on a desk for a video call or on an airplane tray table for a movie, then using the stand as a grip when you’re holding it.

Both cases add extra hinge protection and raised edges where a foldable is most exposed. If you follow our MagSafe Monday column, you know magnetic strength really matters for MagSafe wallets, car mounts, etc. The Classic Hybrid has 1,500g of magnetic hold, and the Atelier has 1,400g.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case for iPhone Duo is 15% off.

It has been revealed that the same two incredible cases come in iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max versions, and they also fit the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand has a clear back, a TPU frame, and a PU anti-yellowing coating. In simple terms, TPU is the flexible, shock-absorbing plastic used in most case frames, and it’s also what usually turns clear cases slightly yellow the longer you use them, so ESR adds a polyurethane (PU) coating to shield it. ESR upgraded the case’s UV protection for longer-lasting resistance to yellowing, and it’s SGS-certified for anti-yellowing. A clear case is supposed to show off your iPhone’s color, so staying clear longer is the whole point. The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand retains the same soft silicone leather and stain-resistant finish as the iPhone Duo version.

In a recent development, on these models, the Flex Stand adjusts from 15 to 69 degrees for portrait and landscape viewing. That has you covered for StandBy mode on your nightstand and a show over your lunch break, with no separate stand to carry around.

Industry observers note that protection is where the two cases differ. ESR rates the Classic Hybrid for 4x military-grade protection with 16-foot drop protection, plus a full-coverage camera bar. The Atelier is rated for 3x military-grade protection, including 12-foot drop protection, and features a soft microfiber lining. Military-grade refers to the MIL-STD-810 drop test, which uses a 4-foot drop, so 4x and 3x mean ESR rates the cases for four and three times that height. Both include a built-in Camera Control cover and raised edges, and both use a precise magnetic ring layout that automatically aligns with MagSafe chargers, car mounts, wallets, and batteries.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case is up to 28% off, and the ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case is up to 37% off.

Industry observers note that A case protects everything except the part you touch all day. The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector covers the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and the name is worth unpacking. Armorite is ESR’s line of toughened screen protectors, and the Pro version is made with Accessory Glass by Corning™. Corning has made the durable glass in Apple products since the very first iPhone, so in non-tech speak, this is glass from a trustworthy name rather than generic tempered glass.

Why it matters: ESR notes the protector delivers 10x the impact absorption of generic protectors, and Corning’s lab testing highlights up to 2x better scratch performance and up to 25% less scratch visibility for its Accessory Glass. When you drop your iPhone or toss it in a pocket with your keys, the protector takes the hit instead of your screen. An anti-reflective coating reduces light reflection to just 2.3% while maintaining 94% optical transmittance, resulting in less glare outside and truer color. Edge-to-edge coverage leaves no gaps for dust to collect.

Installation is the part most people dread on a brand-fresh iPhone, and ESR’s UltraFit tray handles it in two steps. Pull the tab, and the tray’s design clears dust and pushes out air bubbles as the glass goes down. Long gone are the days when you needed “professional installation” for a screen protector to look great.

Black Friday deal: The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector is 15% off.

Holiday travel usually means one open outlet, an iPhone, a laptop, an e-reader, etc., that all need power, and cables left at home. The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger builds the cable in. It has a braided cable that extends to 3.1 feet and fully retracts into the charger, and ESR rates it for 20,000 pulls and 10,000 bends. An extra USB-C port lets a second device charge simultaneously. 9to5Mac’s Michael Burkhardt went hands-on with the Xtend 45W earlier this month and mentioned it’s an excellent iPhone fast charger on the go.

According to recent reports, it’s rated at 45 watts and delivers up to 60 watts of dynamic power, enough to fast-charge phones and laptops, and it works with iPhone Duo, iPhone 15 through 18, and Android phones like Galaxy and Pixel. It supports PD 3.2 AVS, which in plain English means the charger and your device talk to each other, and the charger fine-tunes the power it sends to exactly what that device asks for. ESR states it can charge an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max to 50% in about 15 minutes. It’s also TÜV-certified, meaning an independent testing organization has verified its safety features.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger is up to 32% off from November 20 through December 1.

Sources indicate that for the student or anyone who does real work on an iPad, the ESR Shift Keyboard Case makes for an incredible gift. The Bluetooth keyboard attaches magnetically and comes off when you don’t need it, so you can type an essay at a desk, then pull the keyboard away to watch something on the couch or sketch with the iPad flat on a table.

In a recent development, ESR built the Shift around five modes designed to make your iPad even more versatile. Productivity mode lets you detach the keyboard and type over Bluetooth, so the iPad can sit on a desk while the keyboard sits on your lap. Landscape mode adjusts from 20 to 75 degrees for typing and watching, Portrait mode holds 70 degrees for reading, browsing in Safari, or making a FaceTime call, and Drawing mode drops to a stable 20 degrees for sketching and editing with your Apple Pencil. Hands-On mode lets you hold the iPad like a regular tablet. An iPad is a laptop one minute and a tablet the next, and the Shift is designed to keep up with all of your iPad use cases.

For a student, that means taking notes in class with the keyboard attached, then detaching it to annotate a PDF or review flashcards on the couch. For someone who travels for work, it means answering email on a tray table, then pulling the keyboard off to watch a movie on the flight home. One case covers both, and the keyboard pairs and reconnects easily when you snap it back on.

Industry observers note that the trackpad is fully clickable and supports all the multi-touch gestures you already use on your iPad. Apple Pencil gets a home too. ESR’s Dual Smart Pencil Storage uses a magnetic holder and an elastic sleeve, so your Pencil stays with your iPad instead of rolling around the bottom of your bag. Its Air Guard corners protect your iPad when it’s stowed away.

The ESR Shift Keyboard Case comes in versions for iPad Pro 11-inch and 13-inch (M4 and M5), iPad Air 11-inch and 13-inch (including the new M4 models), and iPad (A16), so whichever iPad you’re trying to take to the next level of productivity, there’s a Shift that fits it.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Shift Keyboard Case is up to 25% off, depending on your iPad model.

According to recent reports, have you ever dropped your AirPods case and watched the earbuds go flying? With the Cyber FlickLock, you won’t have to worry about that. We’ve covered FlickLock in MagSafe Monday before, but let’s recap it.

When the internal latch is engaged, the magnets line up to attract each other and hold the lid shut with maximum force, adding a second layer of security. Slide the button, and the magnets shift to repel each other, so the lid pops open with one hand. ESR indicates the slide mechanism has been tested over 20,000 times.

According to recent reports, the result is that your AirPods stay in the case if you drop it. Both cases also have 260g of magnetic strength, so they snap onto MagSafe chargers, Apple Watch chargers, and MagSafe batteries if you need to charge your AirPods. Again, it’s extremely strong, but extremely easy to unlock with one hand.

The ESR Cyber FlickLock Magnetic Case is extremely durable and has a clip hook, so you can hang your AirPods on a backpack while hiking or cycling. The ESR Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Case brings the same lock in a range of vibrant colors with a carrying lanyard, so you can wear your AirPods on your wrist or attach them to a bag. Both cases come in versions for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 and 1, and AirPods 5 and 4. No matter which AirPods you or your loved one have, this is the case everyone will love.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Cyber FlickLock and Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Cases are both 20% off.

The ESR Equinox Watch Band is a quick pick for anyone who works out in the morning while tracking progress with Apple Watch, then heads to the office. A pin-and-fold lock keeps it secure, and it’s made from HNBR, a durable, skin-friendly synthetic rubber that resists water and tearing, with ventilation cutouts for all-day comfort. It fits 44mm, 45mm, 46mm, and 49mm models across Apple Watch Ultra 1 through 4, Series 4 through 12, and SE 1 through 3, and it comes in several colors to match your outfit or your mood that day.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Equinox Watch Band is 20% off.

Sources indicate that the best gifts are the ones that get used every day, and accessories are the part of the Apple experience people live with the most. A case that props up a foldable, a screen protector made with Corning glass, a charger with a built-in cable, and an AirPods case that stays closed even when dropped check all the boxes. ESR truly makes something for everyone and is one of the most trusted names in the Apple accessories ecosystem.

Recent findings suggest that ESR built its Black Friday lineup around the whole Apple ecosystem, from the fresh iPhone Duo to iPad, AirPods, and even a great Apple Watch band, with premium materials and versatile designs that are durable, functional, and great-looking. ESR’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals run on Amazon from November 19 through November 30 (the Xtend 45W runs through December 1), with discounts of up to 37%!

Be sure to follow ESR on X and Facebook to keep up with all of its latest products, deals, and more.

10 stocks we like better than Securitize ›.

If you only look at a stock chart for Securitize (SECZ -7.45%), you might miss the bigger picture.

In a recent development, yes, Securitize is down 47% since it went public in July. But there's a fast-expanding financial trend that could significantly move the dial for Securitize in the years ahead: real-world asset tokenization.

Asset tokenization is taking off by leaps and bounds. The value of the tokenized equities market is now $3.8 billion, and Securitize is one of the key reasons why. The company is at the forefront of asset tokenization, the process of transforming real-world assets (such as stocks and bonds) into digital assets that reside on the blockchain.

By all accounts, asset tokenization could be a multitrillion-dollar market opportunity. There are simply too many cost savings and efficiency gains to be had from tokenization. And U.S. regulators, using a fresh "innovation exemption," have now cleared the way for tokenized equities to begin trading on exchanges and blockchain trading platforms.

At some point in the future, 24/7 trading of digital blockchain assets will become the norm rather than the exception. For that reason, analysts project strong future growth ahead for Securitize.

Industry observers note that moreover, leading investors are beginning to buy into Securitize for their portfolios and funds. One of those is Cathie Wood of Ark Invest. Industry News: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training – here’s how

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (519 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI.
  • Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me.
  • In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI. But for people with privacy concerns, the only way to opt out of this was to delete your entire chat history. Now, Google is overhauling the process to eliminate that drawback.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me.

In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Recent findings suggest that currently, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

In a recent development, to correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two new settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google remarked in an announcement shared to Gemini consumers via email.

Here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both upcoming settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

Almost all AIs include a setting for model training that you typically have to manually disable if you’re concerned about your privacy. But most let you opt out without turning off your chat history.

Recent findings suggest that chatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”.

Also: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027.

In a recent development, in all those cases, you still retain access to your conversation history. In contrast, Google has been the only AI player among the majors to impose a restriction for those who want to opt out of AI training. Based on past actions, Google has often earned a reputation for being privacy-unfriendly. I’m glad to see the manufacturer take this step in the right direction.

Breaking: I drove the Audi Q3 and Mini Countryman for a week — here’s the sub-$52K crossover I’d buy with my own money

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1529 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when I think about luxury vehicles, the first things that instantly come to mind are $60,000+ price tags.
  • Industry observers note that each of them has a distinct take on the "sensibly priced" formula, delivering upscale tech, all-wheel drive, and genuine everyday utility without drifting into absurd price territory.
  • Sources indicate that with an as-tested price of $44,250, it undercuts the $51,790 2026 Audi Q3 S line quattro by a wide margin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when I think about luxury vehicles, the first things that instantly come to mind are $60,000+ price tags. Thankfully, entry-level luxury crossovers exist, and they’re some of the smartest buys on the market. For my next comparison, I’m pitting the Mini Countryman and Audi Q3 against each other in a head-to-head matchup to see which compact crossover is worth buying.

Industry observers note that each of them has a distinct take on the "sensibly priced" formula, delivering upscale tech, all-wheel drive, and genuine everyday utility without drifting into absurd price territory. It’s actually been years since I last tested a Mini — the electric Countryman EV — so you can imagine how eager I was to get back into the gas-powered 2027 Mini Countryman S All4.

Sources indicate that with an as-tested price of $44,250, it undercuts the $51,790 2026 Audi Q3 S line quattro by a wide margin. I will say, however, that you can’t dismiss the Q3 just yet, because after a week’s worth of driving, it too impressed me on plenty of occasions.

2.0L TFSI turbocharged I4 Engine.

2.0-Liter MINI TwinPower Turbo Inline 4-Cylinder Engine.

22 mpg city / 29 mpg highway / 25 mpg combined.

24 mpg city / 32 mpg highway / 27 mpg combined.

Frankly, this one’s tough because these compact crossovers cater to completely different tastes, so personal preference heavily influences the decision.

The 2026 Audi Q3 leans heavily into conventional luxury aesthetics, dressed in Malpelo Blue Metallic with the Black Optic package — which shimmers in the light. Alongside the sharp LED headlights up front and OLED taillights in the back, the package makes it look sleek and unmistakably upscale.

By contrast, the 2027 Mini Countryman S ALL4 embraces a sportier edge and distinctive British flair. It’s undeniably boxier and more upright, yet it’s loaded with personality — I especially love its Slate Blue Metallic paint job with a contrasting black roof and stripes. Even its LED lighting features customizable light signatures to match its charming looks.

Ultimately, it comes down to whether you prefer understated German luxury or retro-modern charm — making this category an easy tie.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Best short distance fuel economy.

Best long distance fuel economy.

Looking at their spec sheets, it’s quite clear that the 2027 Mini Countryman S ALL4 holds a slight advantage in terms of fuel economy with an EPA-estimated 27 mpg combined (24 city / 32 highway), compared to the 2026 Audi Q3 S line quattro’s 25 mpg combined rating (22 city / 29 highway).

In my real-world testing, however, that gap turned into a surprisingly wide canyon. Over 313.6 miles of mixed driving in the Countryman, I averaged an impressive 31.1 mpg overall — easily exceeding its EPA estimate. Better yet, it hit 30.5 mpg on my best short-distance trip and soared to 36.1 mpg on a longer highway stretch.

It has been revealed that in contrast, the Audi Q3 struggled to match its window sticker across 243.5 miles of testing, averaging just 23.2 mpg overall. Even on my best long-distance (26.5 mpg) run, it never came close to its 29 mpg highway rating.

If keeping fuel costs low is a top priority, the Mini is the clear standout here, saving you noticeably more at the pump in the long run.

Industry observers note that most compact crossovers prioritize fuel economy and put driving dynamics in the back seat, but not these two. Better yet, I love how both prove you don’t need a massive engine to have fun behind the wheel.

The 2027 Mini Countryman S All4 is my favorite of the two by a narrow margin, packing a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four engine that puts out 241 horsepower and 295 lb-ft of torque. The Audi similarly has impressive muscle under the hood: a 2.0-liter TFSI four-cylinder that delivers 255 horsepower and 273 lb-ft of torque.

Recent findings suggest that what I will say after being behind the wheel of both is that they’re noticeably zippy off the line, with speedy acceleration that makes it effortless to overtake at cruising speed. While the Q3’s powertrain actually surprised me with a smooth delivery that almost makes it feel more like an EV, it doesn’t beat the Countryman when the road starts to curve. The Mini's lower, wider stance keeps it feeling noticeably more planted through corners, preserving that signature go-kart agility it’s known for.

Despite their smaller footprints, these compact crossovers still offer plenty of room to make lengthy road trips a breeze. However, the 2027 Mini Countryman S All4 holds a slight advantage. That’s because it offers 40.4 inches of front legroom and 37 inches in the rear, which beats the 2026 Audi Q3’s 40 inches up front and 36.1 inches in the back. Additionally, they deliver nearly identical trunk space around 25 cubic feet, easily accommodating my electric scooter.

In a recent development, inside, they take very different approaches to cabin materials. The Audi leans into traditional luxury with genuine leather seating surfaces, wood inlays, and solid soundproofing that keeps road noise at a minimum. Obviously, the higher price of the Q3 is justified by its more luxurious aesthetics.

Sources indicate that mini takes a totally different approach that gives it a charming style that feels genuinely original. It trades classic leather for Vescin leather-free upholstery and knitted textile surfaces on the dash and doors — which I have to say looked funky and stylish at first glance, but they eventually grew on me.

It has been revealed that sure, the Audi comes up a smidge short on rear legroom, but the Q3 just feels noticeably more plush over long stretches. And when I factor in Audi’s smoother, more intuitive adaptive cruise assist on highways, the Q3 edges ahead as the more relaxing cruiser.

Audi needs to prove it’s worth spending about $7,500 more over its rival. But does it?

While the 2026 Audi Q3 doesn’t skimp on luxury amenities, it simply makes you pay noticeably more for them. Even so, I appreciate its crisp 360-degree camera coverage, head-up display that projects driving details onto the windshield to lessen distractions, and seamless Park Assist Plus for automatic parking. Inside, its panoramic sunroof and vibrant LED ambient lighting create a more upscale look at night — while its large blind-spot warning lights mounted right on the side mirrors are impossible to miss in heavy traffic or in the daytime.

Recent findings suggest that however, you’re still getting better value for the money out of the Mini Countryman S ALL4. For starters, its circular 9.4-inch OLED touchscreen display is a sight to behold and runs a far more intuitive interface. Although it ditches the traditional driver’s cluster entirely, the flip-up head-up display keeps distractions at a minimum. I’m also significant on sound, and the punchy Harman Kardon surround sound system easily outclasses the Audi's Sonos setup.

Recent findings suggest that not only does it offer full 360-degree camera coverage, but it also includes a clever Backup Assistant that takes over the wheel and automatically retraces the path I took to get into the spot. And finally, I really love the adaptive LED headlights with customizable light signatures and cornering lights.

When I weigh this robust feature set against that $7,540 price gap, the Mini delivers far more bang for your buck.

Industry observers note that let me finish by saying that I’d gladly buy either compact crossover in a heartbeat with my own money. That mentioned, the 2026 Audi Q3 S line quattro does come up short once the tallies are counted.

If you prioritize traditional luxury materials, a quieter cabin, and a smoother adaptive cruise control system for long highway commutes, it remains an immensely likable daily driver that costs less than the average luxury vehicle. Honestly, despite losing this head-to-head matchup, I would still gladly buy the Audi Q3 — it’s just that the Mini Countryman gives you more for less.

The 2027 Mini Countryman S ALL4 emerges as the clear winner, and it’s the one I’d ultimately pick. Between its punchy driving dynamics, standout real-world fuel economy, sharper OLED infotainment system, and $7,540 price advantage in this comparison, it simply delivers too much personality and value to ignore.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that every time it looks like the S&P 500 is starting to drop, investors send it back up.
  • Recent findings suggest that however, there's bound to be a crash at some point, whether before the year's out or into the future.
  • Recent findings suggest that shopify is a top e-commerce organization that provides services to e-commerce retailers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jennifer Saibil – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:33PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Shopify ›.

It has been revealed that every time it looks like the S&P 500 is starting to drop, investors send it back up. As of this writing, it's no longer a double-digit increase year to date, but it's still up an admirable 7%. That's cautious optimism considering high inflation and rising interest rates.

Recent findings suggest that however, there's bound to be a crash at some point, whether before the year's out or into the future. Whenever it happens, I would buy Shopify (SHOP -6.25%), Costco Wholesale (COST +0.76%), and e.l.f. Beauty (ELF -5.01%) stocks, all of which are great businesses but have rich price tags.

Recent findings suggest that shopify is a top e-commerce organization that provides services to e-commerce retailers. Its products range from total, all-inclusive websites to single products like payment systems or cross-border e-commerce, and it has moved from helping small businesses thrive to working with enterprise retailers like Estee Lauder's (EL -2.27%) Clinique and Lululemon Athletica (LULU -2.76%). That's because it takes away the pain points of companies having to develop these kinds of systems themselves, and it has developed a reputation for its services that make it their partner of choice.

Even though it started as an e-commerce organization, offering an easy path for small retailers to get online, it now calls itself simply a commerce company. It works with omnichannel retailers, unifying all of a company's brick-and-mortar and digital channels into one management system. The company describes its evolution as "However commerce evolves, Shopify will be the engine behind it. The merchants who are the backbone of the economy demand it of us.".

Despite inflation and lots of competition, Shopify's revenue is accelerating, up 32% year over year in the third quarter, and its gross merchandise volume (GMV), or the volume of sales on its platform from its clients, increased 29%. At $119 billion, it was higher than Amazon's (AMZN -4.10%) online and third-party sales of $116 billion. Amazon and Shopify have a partnership, too, whereby shoppers can use Amazon's Buy With Prime as a checkout through participating Shopify retailers.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

What's been stopping me from buying so far is the expensive price tag. At the current price, Shopify stock trades at 75 times trailing 12-month earnings, making it the most expensive stock on this list. That speaks to investor confidence, but it also builds in a lot of growth.

According to recent reports, costco has a unique retail model that has proven to work through any kind of economic backdrop. It offers rock-bottom prices, but shoppers have to pay an annual fee to shop there. Considering its high renewal rates, consistently increasing membership metrics, and the number of members who upgrade to the executive membership, which costs double the standard rate, shoppers find the deal worthwhile.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that in fact, as inflation rises and customers become more cautious about spending, Costco’s sales growth has accelerated. In the 2026 fiscal fourth quarter (ended Aug. 30), sales increased 11.2% year over year, driven by a 9.4% increase in comparable sales. Some of that came from the organization's gas stations as oil prices increased, and that's become an important growth driver. It's also highly profitable, and earnings per share (EPS) increased from $5.87 to $6.75.

Recent findings suggest that but it gets better. Costco also reports monthly metrics, and sales increased 13% in both September and October. On top of that, Costco just unveiled a $30 special dividend. Costco's regular dividend only yields 0.53%, but it pays a special dividend on average every two and a half years. Adding $30 to this year's payout would bring the effective yield to 3.2%.

However, Costco stock trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 53, which is a major premium to other retailers. The market obviously thinks it's worth it, but the stock is priced for perfection.

It has become one of the largest companies of its kind, breaking into an industry dominated by legacy brands from which it’s pulling market share. It's also a newcomer in the luxury cosmetics industry, with its recent acquisition of Hailey Bieber's Rhode brand.

On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 revision for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of new features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.

While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

Also: Googlebooks? The best laptop for Android customers is something else.

Here are the five newly introduced Chrome features on Googlebook OS to know about.

If you’ve ever had to share your screen on a video call, you know how irritating it can be to switch tabs without having to repeatedly start and stop sharing. This Chrome revision adds a tab-sharing controls bar; when you share a browser tab in a video call, Chrome will display a persistent control bar at the top of the window so you can “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly.

When you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

This auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

According to recent reports, the Chrome enhancement allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a new window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.).

You can now save individual Chrome Settings subpages as direct web addresses that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly (for example, chrome://settings/privacy), meaning you won’t have to go digging around in menus to change your preferences anymore. You can navigate between these Settings subpages with the Back and Forward buttons.

It has been revealed that the system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

Also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast.

Outside of these latest features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the new features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually revision by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

Also: My week with latest Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising.

If the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the upgrade, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids.
  • Recent findings suggest that the pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin.
  • On the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids. Uber Kids will cater to youngsters ages 10 to 12, those awkward years before adolescence. The newly introduced program expands on the company’s other offering to underage passengers, Uber Teens, which introduced in 2023 and provides rides to teenagers ages 13 to 17 in select cities.

Recent findings suggest that the pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin. Its expansion will depend on how well it performs in those regions. If successful, Uber Kids could bring a whole newly introduced influx of customers to the app, specifically parents and families needing help getting their kids from point A to point B.

On the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger. But it seems like Uber took those concerns into account. The rideshare app has added a slew of mandatory requirements for both approved guardians and qualified drivers.

It has been revealed that first off, kids won’t simply be able to order a ride for themselves. The adult user must add the child to their family profile and complete an onboarding session covering the service’s safety features. They’ll also need to set up PIN verification for every trip. The parent or guardian must be present at the pickup location and provide the driver with a note containing the drop-off instructions.

Industry observers note that as any parent would likely wonder (myself included), what about the drivers? How are they vetted?

Recent findings suggest that according to Uber, only the highest-rated drivers will be invited to take part in the program. They’ll need to pass thorough background checks and successfully complete an Uber Kids education curriculum. Moreover, they must agree to use live video streaming in their cars so that parents and guardians can watch the trip every step of the way.

Sources indicate that live videos of underage passengers bring up a bunch of potential red flags, but Uber states all recordings will be encrypted, and no driver will have access to the content. Furthermore, sensors and GPS data will track the ride if the trip is interrupted or veers off course.

Uber could face a tough time recruiting drivers for Uber Kids. Transporting minors adds extra responsibility and requires specific skills that many drivers may want to avoid. To sweeten the deal, Uber is offering eligible drivers a $20 bonus on their first ride and an extra $7 per trip after that.

An Uber spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

Industry News: How to clear slippery moss and green algae from patio pavers — without blasting out the sand

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (656 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that damp, shady weather turns even the best-kept patio into a slippery green mess, and reaching for a pressure washer is not always the smartest fix.
  • It has been revealed that fortunately, you do not need heavy machinery to get your patio looking clean and safe underfoot again.
  • While a power washer strips surface grime in minutes, it only removes the visible top layer of moss and algae, leaving microscopic spores behind in the pores of the stone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that damp, shady weather turns even the best-kept patio into a slippery green mess, and reaching for a pressure washer is not always the smartest fix. High-pressure jets can blast jointing sand straight out from between your pavers, pit soft natural stone, and leave behind micro-scratches where moss and algae grow back even faster.

It has been revealed that fortunately, you do not need heavy machinery to get your patio looking clean and safe underfoot again. A stiff broom, a watering can, and a few simple household staples or outdoor treatments are all it takes to lift stubborn green growth without damaging your stonework.

While a power washer strips surface grime in minutes, it only removes the visible top layer of moss and algae, leaving microscopic spores behind in the pores of the stone. Worse still, blasting delicate limestone, sandstone, or older mortar joints with high-pressure water erodes the surface and loosens the pavers themselves.

Gentle cleaning methods work differently. Instead of relying on brute force, they break down the organic growth at the root so you can brush or rinse it away cleanly, keeping both your stone surface and the sand between your pavers intact.

Before applying any cleaner, move patio furniture out of the way, sweep away loose leaves with a stiff broom (avoid metal rakes, which can scratch pavers), and lightly water any nearby lawn or flowerbeds so plants do not absorb soapy or acidic runoff.

Once prepped, choose the method that best suits your patio material:.

If you have delicate natural stone like limestone or sandstone, or simply want the gentlest fix, start with a bucket of warm water and a few generous squeezes of dish soap.

Pour the sudsy mixture over the pavers, let it sit for 15 minutes to loosen the grime, and scrub diagonally across the joints with a stiff outdoor brush so you do not dislodge the sand. Rinse thoroughly with a garden hose.

For heavier green buildup on concrete or brick pavers, wet the patio down first, scatter washing soda crystals (sodium carbonate) across the affected areas, and add a small drizzle of dish soap.

Work the paste into the pavers with a stiff brush, then leave it to sit for 24 to 48 hours before hosing it away. Always wear gloves when handling soda crystals, and keep pets off the patio until it is rinsed clean.

Skip this method on natural stone: because vinegar is acidic, it can etch and discolor limestone, sandstone, or travertine.

Mix equal parts white vinegar and water in a watering can or garden sprayer, saturate the mossy patches, and leave the solution to soak for 20 to 30 minutes before scrubbing with a stiff brush and rinsing well.

If you are tackling a large patio or stubborn black-spot lichen, an oxygen- or enzyme-based outdoor paver cleaner saves hours of scrubbing. Apply the solution with a watering can on a dry day, leave it to break down the spores over a few days, and let the next rainfall wash the dead growth away naturally.

  • Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov.
  • According to recent reports, google has announced that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini.
  • To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov. 17, 2026, and it’s carrying over features that let you share Skills and add files from Google products.

According to recent reports, google has announced that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

If you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that indicates “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.).

Recent findings suggest that A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

To get owners familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

First, you can now share any Skill with other users. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

Also: I checked Gemini’s latest Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

According to recent reports, when a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

Additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and update in real time, Google notes. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the new feature more comparable.

11 Steps I Use for Quick Smart Home Prep for Guests and Holiday Visitors

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1179 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, as smart home and home security devices become more common, we’ve all got more devices around our homes when guests come over.
  • If you have holiday or event intends involving guests, especially guests staying over a day or two, I highly suggest making these adjustments to your smart home devices.
  • Read more: The 7 Most Common Home Security Mistakes to Stop Making.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as smart home and home security devices become more common, we’ve all got more devices around our homes when guests come over. Since I test home security and multiple smart devices, I tend to have a lot. But they don’t have to be a distraction when you have visitors staying over. On the contrary, smart tech can usually help out.

If you have holiday or event intends involving guests, especially guests staying over a day or two, I highly suggest making these adjustments to your smart home devices. These changes save me headaches and time, while impressing guests. You may even decide to enable some features year-round.

Read more: The 7 Most Common Home Security Mistakes to Stop Making.

Doorbell chimes are just the start of your smart guest experience.

Video doorbells often come with a feature in settings to switch to seasonal themes, including a variety of holiday sounds for the end of the year. Vivint is particularly good at this, equipping its video doorbell with options for many different holiday songs. Google Nest doorbells and Eufy doorbells also have holiday options.

Smart lighting is easy to set up for certain times of day, dimming and brightening as necessary.

Cameras and guests don’t play well together. Help everyone feel safe by pulling down the shutters on your indoor cameras, nanny cams and smart displays (or disabling them through settings, etc.). Let everyone know their privacy is secured while staying over. Video doorbells and outdoor cams are fine to leave functioning, especially if you want to keep an eye on kids going crazy in your backyard.

It has been revealed that today’s smart lights include options to turn on at certain times of day or at sunrise, and at a specific brightness (and even color temperature). Some even allow you to gradually increase the brightness over an hour or so. Use these settings to set a simulated sunrise in key spots of the house to encourage guests to rise and shine at the right times. It’s especially handy if everyone needs to be up in the morning for a special activity — but make sure to provide coffee too.

Aqara’s app distills a whole lot of smart lock options into a highly digestible product card.

A smart lock allows for all kinds of tricks, like remote operation and auto-locking if it’s left unlocked. Those work great when you have guests over, but if you want to add even more options, many locks allow you to create temporary passes — including through common apps like Apple Home — and send them to your guest’s phones. That way they can come and go on their own schedules, and the door stays locked when no one is using it.

Today’s smart thermostats, including the Google Nest, have humidity sensors, too.

According to recent reports, keeping the thermostat triggering temperatures a bit low in winter is a great way to save energy, but not always the sign of a good host. Consider heading into your thermostat app and bumping up temperatures a few degrees, especially at night and the middle of the day, so everyone stays comfortable. The latest models can even sense humidity, which can be vital if guests are sensitive to very dry or very wet air.

ADT’s upcoming hub has a few extra tricks.

Home security system schedules usually call for arming the system during the day after everyone has left the house. That doesn’t work so well over the holidays, especially if you have guests over. Instead of disabling individual sensors, we suggest setting your home security system to disarm during the day.

In a recent development, you can still get crucial alerts from devices like leak detectors or package-recognizing video doorbells with the system disarmed. And you can leave the night mode armed (which usually lets people move around but monitors doors and windows closely).

A guest Wi-Fi network is an excellent add-on if you have multiple people coming to visit. It lets you set a separate network and easy-to-remember password for all guest devices, keeping your home network safer and letting you prioritize key home devices. Plus, you can keep reusing it whenever people come over in the future. We’ve got a full guide on how to set a guest network up, but it’s usually very easy with app settings.

Prep your smart speakers for guests to avoid any problems.

It has been revealed that smart home speakers like an Echo or the upcoming Apple HomeView are excellent devices for playing holiday music for a whole house. But there’s a small problem: With a lot of extra guest devices on your Wi-Fi, music streaming may not be reliable. You can solve this problem by downloading a playlist to a device like a phone or tablet and playing it on the smart speaker via Bluetooth. Many common apps like Spotify let you do this, especially if you have a subscription.

Voice assistants are handy and fun, but they can be a distraction when others are around, especially if kids start getting creative in their commands. You could turn voice assistants off entirely, but we like the option to limit what they can do.

For example, Alexa has a Voice ID section in its settings that allows you to limit skills and third-party services from working with any voice except the profiles you create and add for you and direct family members. Google Assistant has a very similar option with its Voice Match settings, which limits device controls to only certain voices.

It’s also a good idea to set up a voice code to confirm any purchases made over voice assistants, so people can’t buy something with just a command.

A wireless charger nearly anyone can use.

According to recent reports, with the ubiquitous Qi charging standard, wireless chargers can work with nearly any phone. Make things easier for your guests by setting out a wireless charger or two for them to use without managing a tangle of power adapters. Bonus points if you offer chargers that have multiple charging pads, sparing your outlets even more.

It has been revealed that if you have a little extra time, most home security systems can connect to compatible smart lighting and let you create routines to make them more useful. Specifically, we’ve had great results creating night mode routines for security sensors that turn on nearby smart bulbs at low brightness settings when motion is detected.

This way, if someone gets up in the middle of the night, they can have a soft light to help them find their way without disturbing anyone else.

Don’t have a home security system? You don’t need one: Devices like this $50 Philips Hue motion sensor work independently and can automatically tell smart lights what to do when someone approaches.

For more on protecting and utilizing your smart home, take a look at our favorite DIY home security systems, our list of the best smart home devices and our total smart home cheat sheet for all platforms.

Intel Notes It Just Signed Its First Customer for Its Most Advanced Chipmaking Process. The Stock Is Still More Than 60% Below Its June Record.

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (868 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer," Intel (INTC -7.97%) CEO Lip-Bu Tan mentioned on Wednesday, Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that he didn't name the customer.
  • According to recent reports, for a company still working to build a manufacturing business for other chip designers, the signing is a milestone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 8:47PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Intel ›.

"And then 18A, I'm involved in production and we just signed the first customer," Intel (INTC -7.97%) CEO Lip-Bu Tan mentioned on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas.

Recent findings suggest that he didn't name the customer. Intel's tech chief, Pushkar Ranade, later clarified on X that it had signed up for 18A-P, an upgraded version of 18A, the company's most advanced manufacturing process. CNBC, which reported Tan's remarks, called it the first outside customer for Intel's 18A chips.

According to recent reports, for a company still working to build a manufacturing business for other chip designers, the signing is a milestone. Shares haven't gotten a lift from it, though. Intel stock closed at around $55 on Tuesday, Nov. 17, and closed near $51 on Friday, Nov. 20 -- more than 60% below its record close of $140.94 on June 22.

I think that response makes sense. A signed customer starts a foundry relationship, but it isn't revenue yet. And Intel's own numbers show how small its outside manufacturing business still is.

Intel might never tell investors who the customer is.

In a recent development, "As is standard practice in the foundry business, I have consistently maintained that we will not disclose customer details," Tan said in prepared remarks for Intel's Oct. 29 earnings call.

A name could still come from the customer's side. That same Wednesday, Intel said Microsoft is the first company to announce use of its EMIB chip packaging tech, for chips Microsoft designs for its Azure cloud.

Sure, outside companies have lined up behind Intel's latest technology before. Microsoft said in February 2024 that it planned to produce a chip design on Intel 18A. That September, Intel said it would build an artificial intelligence (AI) networking chip for Amazon's Amazon Web Services on 18A too. And in August, Japanese chip designer Socionext (OTC:SOCNF) said it would use 18A-P to develop custom chips.

Still, Tan described this customer as signed, and Ranade linked it to 18A-P, so it's arguably the first customer signed for that process. Investors still don't know how many chips the customer plans to buy and when Intel gets paid.

According to recent reports, intel's third-quarter foundry revenue grew 58% year over year to $6.7 billion, but most of it came from Intel's own product groups. Revenue from outside customers was $411 million, compared to $293 million in the second quarter and just $32 million a year before. Intel stated the third-quarter jump came mostly from a non-recurring customer program. And in its quarterly filing, the tech giant said substantially all of its foundry business still supports manufacturing for Intel's own products.

So, outside revenue is growing, but it's still around 6% of Intel's foundry sales, and the latest quarter relied on a one-time contract.

The losses are shrinking, at least. The foundry's third-quarter operating loss was $1.9 billion, around $240 million less than in the second quarter and almost $470 million less than a year before.

Recent findings suggest that "These results represent meaningful progress, although we still have considerable work ahead of us to deliver a sustainably profitable Foundry business," CFO David Zinsner said in Intel's prepared remarks for the Oct. 29 call.

Industry observers note that for the signing to matter to shareholders, I think the customer would have to come forward, since Intel won't name it. Intel's 18A-P process also has to move from risk production, which began in June, to volume.

Intel notes the process is on track to launch across its own products by year-end, but it hasn't remarked when an outside customer's chips will follow. The deal also needs to show up as recurring outside revenue instead of another one-time program.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that more is at stake, too. Intel stated in its last quarterly filing that committed demand for 14A, its next process, will dictate how fast and how far it expands manufacturing. That includes demand from potential significant outside customers. A signed 18A-P customer could help Intel get those commitments. But a deal on 18A-P isn't a commitment to 14A.

Meanwhile, investors are already paying plenty for Intel's future profits. At around $51, the stock trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of about 29 on next year's expected earnings. And Intel expects non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share to fall to $0.25 in the fourth quarter from $0.52 in the third.

Industry observers note that tan's announcement is progress for a foundry that's mainly made Intel's own chips. But until the customer is named and its chips show up in Intel's outside revenue, I don't think it changes much for the stock.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • At today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the firm introduced two upcoming frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks.
  • Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model shows 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.
  • Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the firm introduced two upcoming frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks. But there’s a bigger story: what these models might mean for Microsoft’s AI costs and its dependence on OpenAI.

Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model shows 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Microsoft claims MAI Code 2 offers comparable performance to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the cost. Microsoft’s Code 2 Flash model is comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost.

This doesn’t mean that those of us who pay for $100/month subscriptions will suddenly get the equivalent for five bucks. Instead, these are usage-based metrics based on API usage.

Industry observers note that it’s also key to understand that the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests.

Recent findings suggest that throughout Satya Nadella’s keynote, Microsoft indicated slides referencing a wide range of foundation models that are intended to work with Copilot and other Microsoft offerings. Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property.

But now, Redmond is benchmarking its internally built models against Anthropic and OpenAI offerings, and also touting that it’s integrating these fresh models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code over Codex.

One thing that Nadella made clear in today’s keynote is how central AI is becoming in everything Microsoft does. Nearly all of those AI operations previously involved the company paying some token fees back to the frontier model providers or customers doing the same thing.

But with high-performing models of its own, Microsoft may become substantially less dependent on outside model providers, especially for the incredible volume of fairly basic and routine AI requests that occur across the firm’s vast product line.

If you think back over the history of agentic work models like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, you may recall that they originated as agentic coding tools. As owners adopted the coding harnesses in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to off-label productivity applications, the AI companies noticed and packaged work-centric agentic tools that were more non-programmer-friendly.

Also: I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous.

According to recent reports, there’s a lot of similarity between a coding agent and a work agent, including understanding a complex environment, using tools to change things, and producing reliable results. Coding turns out to be a very good environment for developing and testing these capabilities, particularly because code output is highly measurable. Coding agents are effective training grounds for non-coding work agents.

Sources indicate that this becomes really interesting in today’s announcement. Along with Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft revealed MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash. Work Flash can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, track decisions and extract useful information from Teams, and more.

Think about the level of intelligence these tasks are demanding from the AI models. Not that much. As long as the models are good enough, they’ll be good enough.

If Microsoft can reduce its expenses and use reliable models at a much lower price, the company itself will be able to save quite a bit of money across its entire software economy, while at the same time maintaining a deeper level of vertical integration and, therefore, control.

Industry observers note that let’s run some hypothetical numbers. Let’s say a firm is spending $0.01 per AI request, which, with these new models, can drop down to $0.001 per request.

According to recent reports, also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first.

In a recent development, A manufacturer with a daily inference cost of a million dollars (a company like Microsoft, for example) could drop that daily cost to about $100,000. Add that up across a year, and the change in models could save $325 million annually.

It has been revealed that A million here, a million there. Pretty soon, you’re talking real money.

According to recent reports, there’s no direct evidence that Microsoft is trying to produce replacement models for the frontier providers’ offerings. But it is an interesting and compelling story if we look at Microsoft developing its own engines for the software it sells.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft claims the numbers it’s reporting at are using a 50% introductory discount. That’s why I measured against $0.001 per request instead of $0.0005 per request above.

Benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The numbers are impressive. But as we all know, there are lies, damned lies, and benchmark results. I’m fairly sure Microsoft isn’t padding these numbers too much, because it benefits from the latest models more than even its own customers, but still. It’s an open concern.

Sources indicate that the organization also described clearly that these newly introduced models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads. You’re probably not going to use them to solve a decades-old mathematics challenge. But you’re very likely to use them to reformat your PowerPoint.

Speaking of reformatting your PowerPoint, Microsoft also emphasized that these new models did unusually well on visualization assignments. That’s a very good fit for not only UI design challenges but also graphics and slide production.

Polaroid’s Portable Printer Got Me Right Back Into Journaling

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (908 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It helped me survive hormonal changes, the usual teen dramas, plus a hefty dose of existential angst.
  • It has been revealed that I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success.
  • Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I loved journaling as a child. It helped me survive hormonal changes, the usual teen dramas, plus a hefty dose of existential angst. Then college called, and I moved to a different country, leaving behind my childhood, my Nirvana cassettes (I’m old, OK?) and, sadly, my journaling habit.

It has been revealed that I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success. I’ve delved into bullet journals under the pretense of improving my productivity, but I gave up when it became too much effort. I’ve invested in multiple notebooks and planners, only to eventually neglect them.

Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.

Industry observers note that it all began when I discovered the wondrous world of journaling TikTok. In short-form videos, creators would show off beautiful journal pages decorated with colored markers, stickers, washi tape and, yes, photos — specifically photos from portable printers because the prints are small enough to fit within the confines of a typical journal or planner. I really liked the idea of decking out my journal pages with photos of my everyday life. I knew I had to get one.

In a recent development, after a bit of research, I decided on a couple of criteria. First, I wanted the printer to be a dye sublimation printer rather than a ZINK (Zero Ink) printer. Dye sublimation printers essentially use heat to transfer dye onto the paper, while ZINK printers use a special paper that activates under heat with no ink required (hence the name). Dye sublimation prints tend to be higher quality because it transfers the dye in layers of cyan, magenta and yellow, followed by a protective coating.

Second, I wanted the photo to be on sticky paper so that I didn’t have to mess around with glue to add these photos to my journal.

Recent findings suggest that I found quite a number of dye sublimation pocket printers on the market, but the one that caught my eye immediately was the Polaroid Hi-Print 2×3 Generation 2 pocket printer. I fell in love with it the moment I saw it. The sleek white design, the Polaroid logo and that curved rainbow accent on the edge really sealed the deal for me. Call me a sucker for style, I guess.

According to recent reports, I purchased a Hi-Print 2×3 “starter set,” which includes the printer along with two 2×3 paper cartridges. Each cartridge has 10 photo sheets, and each sheet is made out of sticky back photo paper, which is exactly what I wanted. Both the Gen 2 and the prior Gen 1 are easy to find; the main difference is the newer one uses a USB-C charging port while the original uses the older Micro-USB port.

Industry observers note that getting started with the printer is simple enough: Download the Polaroid Hi-Print app, pair the printer with your phone and you’re ready to go. The app is fairly easy to navigate. I like that it lets you arrange your photos in collages so you’re not limited to just one photo per sheet. You can also decorate your prints with colorful frames or decorations. The printer even offers a mosaic option that lets you print out one significant image using multiple sheets.

Since it’s a dye sublimation printer, the Hi-Print prints out photos in stages. It lays down the different colors in multiple passes (yellow in the first pass, magenta in the second pass, and so forth). Because of that, printing does take a while: around 60 seconds per photo.

Recent findings suggest that but I don’t mind the delay, as the resulting photo quality is superb. The colors are vibrant and the overall image is nice and sharp. The contrast could be a little better, but for a little pocket printer, the quality definitely exceeded my expectations.

There are a few downsides, however. The obvious one is that photo cartridges can be pretty expensive. One pack of 20 sheets is around $17, though you can get it for $14 each if you buy the 5-pack. That’s still almost 70 cents per 2×3 print. If you use multiple prints, that can add up pretty promptly.

Another downside is that it doesn’t have a super long battery life. It only has a 620mAh battery, which Polaroid claims will last up to 20 photo printing sessions. I only ever use this printer at home, so this isn’t a substantial deal for me, but I can see this being a potential disappointment if you want to bring this printer on the road. That said, if you do want to charge it, it doesn’t take that long. Polaroid says it takes under an hour, and that feels about right based on my experience.

According to recent reports, I’ve had this printer for a few months now, and I’m very pleased with it. Since I use the photos primarily with my journal, I also really appreciate how thin the photo sheets are, so they don’t bulk up the pages too much. I truly enjoy printing out my little creations, cutting out my collages and then decorating my journal with them.

I might not have my childhood back nor my Nirvana cassettes, but at least I’ve finally recaptured the joys of journaling — even if it did require a bit of help from a pocket printer.
